'''Edward Davis Jones''' (October 7, 1856 – February 16, 1920)<ref>[https://archive.org/stream/brownalumnimonth208brow/brownalumnimonth208brow_djvu.txt Brown Alumni Monthly, Vol. XX, March 1920]. Retrieved 10 February 2014</ref> was an American [[statistics|statistician]] and [[journalist]].<ref>[http://www.riheritagehalloffame.com/inductees_detail.cfm?iid=544 Rhode Island Heritage Hall of Fame]. Retrieved 16 March 2020</ref> Jones is best known as the "Jones" in the [[Dow Jones Industrial Average]] and as a co-founder of ''[[The Wall Street Journal]].''

== Early life ==
Jones was born on October 7, 1856, in [[Worcester, Massachusetts]]. Jones' parents, Reverend John Jones and Clarissa ({{Nee|Day}}) Jones, were of [[Welsh people|Welsh]] descent.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Conley|first=Patrick T.|title=The Leaders of Rhode Island's Golden Age|publisher=[[The History Press]]|year=2019|location=[[Charleston, SC]]|pages=81|oclc=1119106956}}</ref> Jones graduated from [[Worcester Academy]] and attended [[Brown University]] before dropping out in his junior year.<ref>{{cite news |newspaper=[[The New York Times]]
|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2002/03/31/business/private-sector-kindness-repaid-80-years-later.html
|title=Kindness Repaid, 80 Years Later
|author=Aaron Donovan |date=March 31, 2002}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Rosenberg|first=Jerry Martin|url=|title=Inside the Wall Street Journal: The History and the Power of Dow Jones & Company and America's Most Influential Newspaper|date=1982|publisher=Macmillan|isbn=978-0-02-604860-6|location=|pages=|language=en}}</ref> After leaving Brown, Jones worked as a reporter for the ''Providence Morning Star'' and ''Evening Press'', where he met [[Charles Dow]].

== Dow Jones ==
{{main|Dow Jones & Company}}
The company which is famous for the ''[[Dow Jones Industrial Average]]'', ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' was founded by Jones and [[Charles Dow]] in 1882<ref>{{cite news |newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]]
   |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1999-mar-30-fi-22396-story.html
   |title=A History of the Dow
   |author=Jennifer Oldham |date=March 30, 1999}}</ref> "in the basement of the [[New York Stock Exchange]]";<ref>{{cite news
|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]
|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1984/01/20/business/dow-jones-insures-family-control.html
|title=Dow Jones insures family control
|author=Alex S. Jones  |date=January 20, 1984}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]]
   |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/1997/03/21/with-blue-chips-for-101-years-dow-jones-is-key-market-index/
   |title=With blue chips for 101 years, Dow Jones is key market index 
   |author=Julius Westheimer |date=March 21, 1997}}</ref> [[Charles Bergstresser]] was a silent partner.

Jones had met Dow while both had worked as fellow reporters in [[Providence, Rhode Island]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.riheritagehalloffame.org/inductees_detail.cfm?iid=544|title=Riheritagehalloffame.org|website=www.riheritagehalloffame.org}}</ref> He died in New York in 1920 at the age of 63.
